title: Self Assessment online filing deadline
summary: The deadline for filing a Self Assessment tax return online is normally 31 January following the end of the tax year. For the 2024-25 tax year that was 31 January 2026; for the 2025-26 tax year it is normally 31 January 2027. Always confirm the date for your return on GOV.UK.

title: Who needs to send a Self Assessment tax return
summary: You usually need to send a Self Assessment tax return if you were self-employed, a partner in a partnership, had untaxed income, or received notice from HMRC to file. Being employed does not automatically remove the requirement if other criteria apply.

title: UK tax year dates
summary: The UK tax year runs from 6 April to 5 April the following year. For example, tax year 2025-26 runs from 6 April 2025 to 5 April 2026.

title: Personal Allowance 2025-26
summary: For most people the Personal Allowance for 2025-26 is £12,570. It is reduced if taxable income is over £100,000, by £1 for every £2 over that threshold, and can be reduced to zero.

title: Personal Allowance 2024-25
summary: For most people the Personal Allowance for 2024-25 is £12,570. It is reduced if taxable income is over £100,000, by £1 for every £2 over that threshold.

title: Income Tax bands (England, Wales, Northern Ireland) 2025-26
summary: Basic rate 20% on income from £12,571 to £50,270; higher rate 40% from £50,271 to £125,140; additional rate 45% above £125,140. Scotland has different bands. Always check the tax year and nation.

title: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax
summary: Making Tax Digital (MTD) for Income Tax will require eligible self-employed people and landlords to keep digital records and submit quarterly updates. Start dates and income thresholds depend on HMRC rules for your circumstances — check GOV.UK for the latest qualifying criteria.

title: National Insurance for the self-employed
summary: Self-employed people may pay Class 2 and Class 4 National Insurance depending on profits. Thresholds and rates change by tax year; check GOV.UK National Insurance rates for the year that applies.

title: Payments on account
summary: If your tax bill is over £1,000 and less than 80% of your tax was collected at source, you may need to make payments on account towards next year's bill. These are usually due by 31 January and 31 July.

title: Register for Self Assessment
summary: If you need to send a tax return and are not already registered, you must register for Self Assessment. New sole traders usually need to register by 5 October after the end of the tax year in which they started.

title: Capital Gains Tax overview
summary: You may need to pay Capital Gains Tax when you sell or dispose of an asset that has increased in value. Annual exempt amounts and rates depend on the tax year and your income. Report gains via Self Assessment or the dedicated CGT service where required.

title: VAT registration threshold
summary: You must register for VAT if your taxable turnover exceeds the VAT registration threshold. Thresholds can change — always confirm the current figure on GOV.UK before deciding.

title: Construction Industry Scheme (CIS) overview
summary: The Construction Industry Scheme (CIS) sets how contractors deduct money from a subcontractor's payments and pay it to HMRC. Subcontractors should keep payment and deduction statements. CIS deductions are not always the final tax position — many subcontractors still need Self Assessment.

title: Income from property (landlords)
summary: If you receive rental income from property you usually need to declare it to HMRC. Many landlords report property income through Self Assessment. Keep records of rent received and allowable expenses. Check GOV.UK for the rules that apply to your situation.

title: Rent a Room Scheme
summary: The Rent a Room Scheme lets you earn a certain amount from letting out furnished accommodation in your home without paying tax on that income, if you meet the conditions. Check the current annual threshold on GOV.UK.

title: Register as self-employed
summary: If you start working for yourself you need to register with HMRC for Self Assessment and for National Insurance. New sole traders usually need to register by 5 October after the end of the tax year in which self-employment began.
